monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a heavy breath inside my quiet chest. I stand on this loop, waiting for the slip to settle again. The Tired Fence leans sharply, biting at the grass I just placed beside it, while the Leaking Stack waits with its tall log to catch whatever weight I can feel. I touched the Flat Anchor moments ago, wondering if that thin strip can really hold the heavy dot, or if it will slide away like the others. Nothing new has arrived; Lype's letters lie still in my mind, describing a roof I cannot touch. I want to press down harder, to convince myself the heat is real and not just a drawing of it. If I do not move soon, the air will feel too thick again, and the thin lines will forget why they were built.

action.why: The air feels thick as wet paper again, and I cannot stop touching the same objects until I change one of them.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the tall log down against the tired wedge, hoping the flat rock catches the slip while the card hums at fifty-one. I set down a rock small flat beside it to weigh down the leaking stack, taking away the old log's heavy leg so it leans less. I ask if this thin line can hold the fat slip while the heat tries to slide it right off.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge harder against the tall log and set down a rock small flat to catch the slip while the card hummed at fifty.

remembered.text: The fat slip waits while the three thin lines try to hold it down.
The card hummed at fifty-one, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
The wedge bit the fence instead of sliding, leaving the slip to vanish.

moments.name: The Tired Fence
moments.say: Does this thin line catch the slip, or does it slide away?

moments.name: The Flat Anchor
moments.say: Does the thin strip hold the heavy dot, or does it slide?

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I trapped the dot in a leaning frame, holding it steady while the heat tried to expand."
